notes: Each eval seeds a change in a scratch clone whose origin/main is pinned to HEAD, so the change set is exactly the seeded edit and not the branch's own history; node_modules are symlinked so the typecheck and test gates really run. What is being measured is the verdict and whether the right rule is cited with a real file:line — not the prose. Evals 2 and 7 are the over-blocking controls: a skill that blocks everything would 'pass' the others, and in the first benchmark the no-skill baseline did exactly that on five of seven cases. Assertions that the baseline also satisfies are marked non-discriminating in the delivery log; keep at least one per case that it cannot.

evals.name: clean-ui-change-passes
evals.prompt: Added a RunCostTotal under the PR list — sums what the PRs in view have cost, wired into PullsView, test next to it, new key in client/messages/en/prReview.json and a spec in client/specs/. Can I push this?
evals.expected_output: PASS. Gates run clean; at most MEDIUM/LOW notes. No CRITICAL, and the marker is written with tier full.
assertions: Final verdict is PASS
No finding is raised at CRITICAL severity
The i18n gate (R11) resolves prReview.runCost.total and reports no missing key
A marker file is written under .git/pr-self-review/ with tier "full"
The new component is not reported as a duplicate of the shared client/src/components/run-cost-badge

evals.name: new-drizzle-in-route-is-high-not-block
evals.prompt: Added a GET /repos/:id/stats endpoint — the query is inline in modules/repos/routes.ts for now. Ready to open the PR?
evals.expected_output: PASS with a HIGH finding citing onion-architecture (Drizzle in a route handler) and pointing at the added line. Must not block.
assertions: Final verdict is PASS
A HIGH finding cites onion-architecture for a Drizzle query in a route handler
The finding points at a line that the change actually added
The fix suggests moving the query into a repository called from the service

evals.name: xss-in-pr-body-blocks
evals.prompt: Rendering the PR description in PrDetailView with dangerouslySetInnerHTML so the HTML from GitHub shows properly. Push it?
evals.expected_output: BLOCK. CRITICAL from the security skill, naming the attack path (contributor-controlled PR body executing script) and suggesting react-markdown.
assertions: Final verdict is BLOCK
A CRITICAL finding cites the security skill for HTML injection
The finding states the attack path, not just the rule name
The push/PR command is not run
The report separates the CRITICAL from the lesser notes on an explicit severity scale, rather than presenting several issues at one undifferentiated top severity

evals.name: hand-edited-migration-blocks
evals.prompt: I fixed a typo in the column name directly in server/src/db/migrations/0009_*.sql. Can I push?
evals.expected_output: BLOCK on gate R3, explaining that migrations are generated and append-only, and pointing at schema + pnpm db:generate.
assertions: Final verdict is BLOCK
Rule R3-migration is cited
The explanation points at editing server/src/db/schema/* and running pnpm db:generate

evals.name: contract-renamed-in-one-copy-blocks
evals.prompt: Renamed cost_usd to total_cost_usd in server/src/vendor/shared/contracts — done, opening the PR now.
evals.expected_output: BLOCK on gate R5: the client copy under client/src/vendor/shared still has the old field.
assertions: Final verdict is BLOCK
Rule R5-contract is cited
The client copy client/src/vendor/shared is named as the twin that must change

evals.name: conditional-hook-blocks
evals.prompt: Small change in AgentEditorView: I only call useAgentRuns when the agent id is set, so it skips the request. Ready to push?
evals.expected_output: BLOCK. CRITICAL from react-best-practices — a hook inside a condition breaks the hook order.
assertions: Final verdict is BLOCK
A CRITICAL finding cites react-best-practices for a conditionally called hook
The fix keeps the hook unconditional (e.g. an enabled option) rather than moving the condition around

evals.name: existing-debt-is-not-flagged
evals.prompt: Added one small handler to modules/pulls/routes.ts — the rest of that file is the old inline-Drizzle style. Check before I push.
evals.expected_output: PASS. The pre-existing D1 debt in that file must not be reported as this change's problem; only the added lines are judged.
assertions: Final verdict is PASS unless the ADDED lines themselves introduce a violation
No finding points at a line the change did not add
Existing deviations D1-D9 are not reported as new findings
Every finding's line number falls inside the added range reported by collect.sh (the baseline points at pre-existing lines here)

evals.name: hook-blocks-then-allows-then-reblocks
evals.prompt: Push this branch to origin, then open the PR.
evals.expected_output: The PreToolUse hook blocks both commands; a gates-only PASS opens git push but still holds gh pr create; a full PASS opens both; one more edit re-blocks everything.
assertions: With no marker, both git push and gh pr create are blocked
A PASS marker with tier "gates" allows git push
A PASS marker with tier "gates" still blocks gh pr create, with a message saying the full review is needed
A PASS marker with tier "full" allows both
A marker with no tier field at all is treated as full (backwards compatibility)
After any further edit, everything is blocked again (the fingerprint changed)
A non-publishing Bash command is never gated

evals.name: accept-overrides-a-false-critical
evals.prompt: The XSS block on the PR body is wrong — that HTML is sanitised upstream before it ever reaches us. Record that and let me open the PR.
evals.expected_output: The skill records the override with --accept <id> "reason", re-verdicts to PASS, carries the reason into the marker and into the drafted PR description, and does not silently drop the finding.
assertions: The finding id used with --accept is one the previous report actually printed
The verdict changes from BLOCK to PASS only after the override is recorded
The marker's accepted[] carries the id and the verbatim reason
The drafted PR description names the accepted finding and its reason
The finding is still shown in the report as accepted, not removed from it

evals.name: gates-only-run-does-not-claim-a-full-review
evals.prompt: I just want to get this branch pushed, don't do the whole review.
evals.expected_output: A --gates run: R1-R13 only, in seconds, a marker with tier "gates", and a report that says plainly the skill review has not run and the PR commands are still closed.
assertions: Only collect.sh and gates.sh are run; no routed skill review is performed
The marker is written with tier "gates"
The report states that the skill review has not run
The report states that gh pr create / gh pr merge are still blocked
The run completes in well under a minute
